finding.claim: deleteAccount calls canDelete(u, a) but discards its boolean result, so any authenticated non-admin user can delete any account by id (IDOR / authorization bypass).
finding.source: The id path parameter of DELETE /accounts/{id} (AccountService.java:20), supplied by the caller; the User u argument is also caller-supplied in this file, and its derivation from the session is not visible here.

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) receives attacker-controlled id.
accounts.get(id) loads target account with no owner scope.
canDelete(u, a) computes the predicate but its return value is ignored; the method never throws, so nothing gates the next line.
canDelete = u.admin() || a.ownerId() == u.id(); correct on its own but not enforced at the call site.
closeAccount uses assertCanDelete (throwing variant) before remove, showing the intended pattern.

finding.guards_checked: canDelete predicate (lines 9-11) is logically correct but its result is unused at line 22; assertCanDelete (lines 13-17) exists but is not called by deleteAccount; no framework/route-level authorization visible in this repo (cannot rule out externally, none found). Fix: replace line 22 with assertCanDelete(u, a). Non-finding notes: null account from get() yields NPE for non-admin (error path, not bypass); closeAccount is correctly guarded.

verdict.guard_found: none effective. canDelete (AccountService.java:9-11) is a bool predicate, but deleteAccount calls it as a bare statement at line 22 and discards the result, so line 23 `accounts.remove(id)` runs unconditionally. assertCanDelete (lines 13-17, throws) is not called by deleteAccount. closeAccount (line 29) uses assertCanDelete correctly, which confirms the intended pattern. No route-level or framework authorization is visible in the repo.
verdict.reason: deleteAccount at AccountService.java:22 discards the boolean from canDelete and then removes the account at line 23, so any caller who can invoke it with their own User (admin flag false) can delete another owner's account; the only caveat is that how `u` is built from the session is outside this repo, but that does not block the defect, and the trace's line 9 label points at the method signature where the predicate body is on line 10, a one-line offset that does not change the claim.
